Undergraduate Recruitment and Admissions contact

Whether you are a prospective student seeking to connect with your recruiter, or a current applicant with specific questions about your application, the Recruitment and Admissions (RAD) Team is here to help!

Join our mailing list Learn how to apply

Ask Rex

Rex can help answer some of your most common questions. If Rex isn’t able to help you, you can connect with one of our advisors by following the instructions below. 

Trending Topics

How to Apply Program Information UCalgary Ranking Find Admission Resources Application Status

Contact the Recruitment and Admissions Team

Answer a few short questions below to be directed to the team that is best suited to support you. 

What type of student are you?
Are you a student with international credentials?
Are you an Indigenous student?
First Nations (status and non-status), Métis, and Inuit
Have you submitted an application for admission this year?
Have you previously studied at a post-secondary institution?
Are you interested in the English Pathway Program prior to starting your degree?

Undergraduate Admissions

We offer advising over the phone and through booked appointments:

  • Contact us by phone if you have multiple questions and/or if your questions are time-sensitive (close to deadlines).
  • Book an appointment if you have a varied or complex academic history, you’d like to discuss the specifics of your admission decision, or if your application wasn’t successful and you’d like to explore next steps.
  • Drop-in appointments are available Monday-Friday from 12:30pm-4pm in the Prospective Student Hub, 2nd floor of the Hunter Student Commons

Phone: 403.210.7625   
Toll free (Canada and USA): 1.855.246.7625   
Fax: 403.220.0762

UCalgary Notice of Collection
The University of Calgary (UCalgary) respects your privacy and is committed to ensuring the privacy of all students, staff, and community members. Your personal information is being collected under the authority of section 4(c) of the Protection of Privacy Act (POPA). It will be collected, used and disclosed for the purposes outlined in UCalgary’s Notice of Collection, Use and Disclosure of Personal Information and managed in accordance with UCalgary’s Privacy Management Program. Your personal information may be input into automated systems to generate content or make decisions, recommendations, or predictions. If you have questions regarding this notice or UCalgary’s collection, use, or disclosure of your personal information, please contact accessandprivacy@ucalgary.ca.

Undergraduate recruiters

Are available on a varied schedule in order to connect with prospective students more easily. 

Meet our recruiters

Visit us for a campus tour 

Get a feel for your campus by signing up for a tour. You’ll visit classrooms, residences and athletic facilities, and receive answers to your most pressing questions.

Your tour guide will be able to answer your questions throughout the tour, or plan to stay for an extra 30 minutes to participate in a group advising session with your peers.

The University of Calgary, located in the heart of Southern Alberta, both acknowledges and pays tribute to the traditional territories of the peoples of Treaty 7, which include the Blackfoot Confederacy (comprised of the Siksika, the Piikani, and the Kainai First Nations), the Tsuut’ina First Nation, and the Stoney Nakoda (including Chiniki, Bearspaw, and Goodstoney First Nations). The city of Calgary is also home to the Métis Nation within Alberta (including Nose Hill Métis District 5 and Elbow Métis District 6).

The University of Calgary is situated on land Northwest of where the Bow River meets the Elbow River, a site traditionally known as Moh’kins’tsis to the Blackfoot, Wîchîspa to the Stoney Nakoda, and Guts’ists’i to the Tsuut’ina. On this land and in this place we strive to learn together, walk together, and grow together “in a good way.”
